exact_statement: For a two-state homogeneous CTMC with X_0=0, rates alpha>0 and beta>0, and horizon T>0, fixing z in (0,1) leaves a continuum of strictly positive rate pairs alpha_lambda=lambda*z/(1-exp(-lambda*T)), beta_lambda=lambda-alpha_lambda for lambda> -log(1-z)/T that all have P(X_T=1)=z but have distinct and strictly increasing expected integrated occupancy I(lambda)=z*(T/(1-exp(-lambda*T))-1/lambda). If two randomized interventions swap two such rate pairs between them, endpoint-only observations of one state per independent founder have identical distributions in both worlds while the intervention maximizing expected integrated occupancy reverses. Any policy then has worst-case regret at least half the occupancy gap. For two specified worlds, one calibrated nondifferential binary observation at an intermediate time tau and n independent founders per arm has sign-test error at most exp(-n*d(tau)^2), where d is the observed-probability gap; a finite grid minimizing the resulting cost provides an executable sufficient design.
assumptions: binary time-homogeneous CTMC with fixed positive rates within each intervention arm
all founders start in verified state 0
interventions are randomized at the independent founder-lineage level
no interference, state-dependent division/death, censoring, or shared-well dependence
the objective is expected integrated state-1 occupancy over a fixed horizon
reporter sensitivity and specificity are known and nondifferential across arms and times
status: conditional theorem internally derived; numeric design finite-grid computation; biological validity and novelty/priority UNKNOWN
novelty_boundary: Does not claim that lineage-based cell-state inference, kin-correlation analysis, CTMC estimation, active timepoint selection, experimental design, or robust POMDP control is new. KCA can infer reversible networks from pedigree correlations and endpoint labels; multi-time population methods and tree-HMM methods use richer channels than the one-founder-endpoint interface here; ICML 2026 already studies active measurement-time selection for measure-valued trajectories, and Bayesian optimal perturbation time design exists for haematopoiesis. The scoped contribution is the explicit action-reversing path-reward alias, minimax endpoint-only regret statement, and finite-grid sensing certificate for this two-state model. No full priority review was done.

reported_example.candidate_design_runtime: O(G) time and O(1) extra memory; local execution completed in under one second
reported_example.initial_state_verification_or_sorting: excluded; charge separately, nominally one baseline read or selection per founder
reported_example.reporter_calibration: excluded; required if sensitivity/specificity are not supplied
reported_example.culture_intervention_imaging_well_and_ba: excluded and must be reported in an actual experiment

costs.sample_bound: n=ceil(log(1/delta)/d^2) independent founders per arm under the two-world sign test and Hoeffding bound; with known nondifferential reporter, d is multiplied by Se+Sp-1

falsifier: The abstract theorem is refuted only by an algebraic error in the CTMC transition law or constructed rate family. The candidate biological model is rejected for a selected system if direct tracks show non-exponential/non-Markov dwell times, state-dependent division/death or censoring changes the observed process, reporter error is arm-dependent/uncalibrated, or replicated data reject the predicted endpoint equality and intermediate separation. In the numeric example the predicted midpoint-grid readout is p_fast=0.4400941 versus p_slow=0.1370682 at tau=0.21215T, while both terminal probabilities are 0.5.
next_gate: Extend the time selector to confidence sets of rates and reporter channels by maximizing worst-case separation across action-reversing model pairs per acquisition cost; return UNKNOWN if every time has zero robust separation. Then compare with KCA/tHMM pedigree-correlation controls under equal founder, imaging/sequencing, and dropout budgets, and include birth/death, censoring, and non-Markov memory.
